notes: The newsdesk's own first held edition: a rumour mill, a taped message from the General's own retirement, and two undercard title matches called live on the broadcast itself (no "roll tape" marker) rather than replayed from elsewhere — the TWIW TV Championship (Hangman over Uncle Nasty by disqualification, no title change) and the TWIW TV Tag Team Championship (the Annihilation Alliance over Carnage in a steel cage rematch). Several further vignettes (Bwana introducing Rasta Batu; Ace Diamond and Fender Marshall's own feud) are explicitly marked "roll tape"/"end tape" and read as taped promo inserts, not fresh in-ring action, and generate angle rather than match appearances. Corrects the wing's own prior tier-1 note, which read the whole broadcast as tape under the anti-double-count rule — a full cold re-read found the two title bouts called live, with no tape marker of their own.

matches.note: TWIW TV Championship. Called live on the broadcast (no "roll tape" marker), not replay. The Hangman clubbed, powerslammed and eventually noosed Uncle Nasty over the top rope before Goliath ran in for the save; the finish is a disqualification, credited to Uncle Nasty as the winner of the match itself, with the newsdesk's own line that "the Hangnail keeps his belt as a result of a disqualification" — the title did not change hands.

TWIW TV Tag Team Championship, a rematch of the tournament final that crowned the champions (not itself held). Called live on the broadcast (no "roll tape" marker), not replay. The Unknown Assailant pinned Burn after a kneedrop from the top of the cage; the Annihilation Alliance retained.

matches.note: Erik and Daemon over Yin and Yang. The finish is a submission: Erik in a full nelson with Daemon lifting Yin’s legs for extra pressure. Afterwards the General handed both Siamese Twins a copy of "Learning English, in Only 10 Minutes a Day."

Decided by outside interference twice over: the Red Baron hit Slimm in the back of the head with a steel chair, and the Hit ‘N’ Run Rabbi ran in dressed as a referee and opened Slimm up with brass knuckles before the real official recovered to make the count.

Six-man tag — the Law and the Grim Reaper against the Maniacs and the Crusher. The Grim Reaper sleepered the Crusher and the referee lifted and dropped his arm three times; he had already carried the Maniacs’ own manager out of the arena in a coffin earlier in the same match.
Fifteen-foot cage, door locked. Frank Steel crawled out for the win after the Neutralizer chased the Savage away from the cage door; both teams were bleeding.
DiMadMan and BudMan over Mr. B and Tom "the Animal" Brown. The Plaid Powerhouse ran in and rolled the paralysed BudMan onto Mr. B for the count.

Two submissions inside a sealed cage, pins and countouts void. One submission each, and then Dr. Down-Under’s own TASER, applied to a chain he had thrown in for the Animal to use, electrocuted the Animal instead when Mr. B emptied a bucket of water over the manager.
The newsdesk’s own anchor came out of retirement to partner the General against the newsdesk’s own colour man. Robby the Lame submitted to the threat of a figure four before the hold was applied.

matches.note: United States Championship. matches.note: A draw as the report declares it.

name: This Week in Wrestling

date.source: The document's own dateline; served as 30 January 1992 under accession lot 0144.

notes: The newsdesk’s own first surviving 1992 edition, and the first document in the held record to print three federations’ standings side by side. Two matches are the wing’s own: a four-team elimination tag rolled from tape of a WeWF Supercard that is not separately held, and a TWIW TV Championship bout called live with a former World Champion as guest announcer. Everything else — a UWF ladies clip, an IWF singles match — belongs to the federation whose card it aired on and is recorded rather than structured.

matches.note: Four-team elimination tag, rolled from tape of a WeWF Supercard not otherwise held. Da Boyz went first (Judge Dredd piledrove Guido), then the Klingons (Klingon Disrupter submitted to a Boston crab), and the Hoosiers beat the Law when Daemon pinned Judge Anderson after a chair the General threw in. "The Law were living by double teaming, and they died by double teaming."

TWIW TV Championship, called live with the General as guest announcer. WINNER AND CHAMPION ARE DIFFERENT MEN: the General left the booth, DDT’d Baron Von Klaw and piledrove him on the concrete, so Mr. B was disqualified and Von Klaw won the match — and "a dazed and surprised Mr. B will keep the belt despite being disqualified." No title change.

name: This Week in Wrestling

date.source: The document's own dateline; served as 15 February 1992 under accession lot 0144.

notes: A television title change and a tag title change, both of them the wing’s own. The rest of the broadcast is the UeWF’s and the IWF’s: a manager interviewed in his own living room, a rival federation’s tag champions cutting a promo in an arena whose power fails on cue, and a manager answering a rumour about a contract on a team’s knees by opening a briefcase and making it true. The UeWF’s own complete rankings across five divisions run at the foot of the issue, with one belt listed vacant.

matches.note: TWIW TV Championship. TITLE CHANGE: the Hangman hung Mr. B over the top rope with his own noose while the referee was down, then hit a flying powerslam off the top turnbuckle. Mr. B had held the belt "for the better part of a month".

WeWF Tag Team Championship, rolled from tape. TITLE CHANGE, the Law’s third reign: Judge Dredd cradled Erik while Machiavelli distracted the referee and Judge Anderson shook the top rope to drop Daemon off it. Mark DeMandable hit the General from behind at ringside.

name: This Week in Wrestling

date.source: The document's own dateline; served as 19 February 1992 under accession lot 0144.

notes: One match of the wing’s own — a television title rematch — around a rumour mill, three taped IWF bouts and, handed to the anchor on a sheet of paper mid-broadcast, a full week of UeWF title results across every belt in that federation, three of them title changes, one of them shown as a clip. Those results are the UeWF’s own and are carried back to that wing’s ledger rather than structured here.

matches.note: TWIW TV Championship. The Hangman retained: a flying clothesline as Mr. B came in for a splash. Both men worked several clean breaks, to the colour man’s open disgust.

name: This Week in Wrestling

date.source: The document's own dateline; served as 25 February 1992 under accession lot 0144.

notes: Four of the wing’s own matches, three of them rolled from tape of a WeWF card. The rest of the broadcast is the IWF’s first Supercard and the UeWF’s title week; the UeWF World Championship change is staged move for move on tape here and is carried back to that wing rather than structured. The editor’s own closing note prints three federations’ commissioners’ account names, which the privacy rule keeps out of the record.

matches.note: TWIW TV Championship. WINNER AND CHAMPION ARE DIFFERENT MEN: Merlin pulled Lancelot out of the way of a clothesline, the Hangman hit the ring post head-on and was counted out, and Lancelot won the match — "the laughs on him though, as the belt only changes hands on a pinfall or submission." No title change.
WeWF United States Championship, rolled from tape. A backslide, and the champion’s perfect record held.
WeWF Tag Team Championship, rolled from tape. Judge Anderson fistdropped Daemon for the count while Da Boss stood at the announce desk counting a briefcase of money out loud.
WeWF World Championship, rolled from tape. Double disqualification: the Inquisition and the Hoosiers all got into the ring, and the General hit Torquemada with the ring bell twice.

name: WeWF Report #50

date.source: The document's own dateline; served as 1 March 1992 under accession lot 0144.

notes: The fiftieth numbered report, and the last weekly report of the league that survives. It opens with a call for players. Nine bouts printed as a bare card, three title matches called at length, and the last World Championship change in the record.

matches.note: United States Championship. A cradle suplex; the champion’s record stayed perfect.
Tag Team Championship, against newcomers billed out of the UFWS. Judge Dredd pinned Paul Cochon after Judge Anderson dropped a knee off the top rope behind the referee’s back.

World Championship, the last title change in the surviving record. TITLE CHANGE: Metal picked the Sandman up over his shoulder and powerslammed him. "Give The Sandman credit, he held that belt for almost a month." The Sandman wrestled with nobody in his corner.

name: This Week in Wrestling

date.source: The document's own dateline; served as 4 March 1992 under accession lot 0144.

notes: The edition with no challenger. A television title match is wrestled without a referee, counted by the challenger’s own manager, and annulled by the championship committee within the hour; a second is then wrestled properly. Three WeWF title bouts are rolled from tape and are the same bouts printed in the wing’s own Report #50 three days earlier — they are structured there, on the card they were wrestled on, and only named here. The Grapplemania ladies match is the UeWF’s own.

matches.note: An unsanctioned TWIW TV Championship match with no referee, counted by Ace Diamond himself. The championship committee declared the bout null and void the same broadcast; the Hangman clotheslined Pruitt over the top rope afterwards and put the noose on Diamond before Cannonball Calhoun and Brimstone Baxter made the save.
TWIW TV Championship, the sanctioned bout. The Hangman rolled him up in an inside cradle after Fitness missed an elbow off the top rope, and kept the belt.
Rolled from tape of a WeWF Supercard not otherwise held. Losing manager’s hair dyed green: Guido DDT’d Flint for the count, and Nunzio sprayed Molly Maguire green afterwards.

name: TWIW TV Tag Team Title Tournament, Round 1

date.source: The document's own dateline; served as 20 March 1992 under accession lot 0144.

notes: Round one of the newsdesk’s own eight-team tournament for a belt it created itself, drawn from four federations — the reigning tag champions of the WeWF, the UeWF and the IWF plus at-large entries. The line that dates the end of a whole federation is in the commentary: two of the entrants are billed as coming from "the now extinct UeWF."

matches.note: A disputed finish the broadcast argues about on air: both teams covered at once, the count went to three, one announcer called it for the Law — "and the ref’s raising the hands of Pruitt and Steele!" The referee’s decision stands and Steele and Pruitt advance.
Won on a shovel shot to Hate while the referee was clearing the ring. Both teams are billed as coming out of the now-extinct UeWF.
Klingon Phaser put a figure four on Action Man; Action Man passed out rather than submit and Mr. B threw in the towel.
Over in seconds: Flint ducked a tie-up and hit a reverse roll-up on Sly.
Lurch clotheslined Jack "The Texas Tornado" Rubenstein while Rubenstein was trapped in the corner.

name: TWIW TV Tag Team Title Tournament, Round 2

date.source: The document's own dateline; served as 24 March 1992 under accession lot 0144.

notes: Four quarter-finals. A table is broken by a flying headbutt in front of the announce desk, and the finish of the first match is a countout the announcers have to correct each other about on air.

matches.note: Won by countout after Burn put Steele through the announce table with a flying headbutt off the top rope. Both men were counted out on the floor, but Crash was the legal man, so Carnage advance.
A double team behind the referee’s back while Bwana distracted him; Klingon Phaser was outside powerslamming the manager.
Flint pinned the Dark Horse on a flying tackle after Aries Prime took his own partner’s axehandle and went over the top rope.
Gomez off Lurch’s shoulders with a flying legdrop onto Destruction. Steelgrave carried Uncle Fester to the back mid-match after Fester hit him with a shovel and it had no effect.

name: TWIW TV Tag Team Title Tournament, Round 3

date.source: The document's own dateline; served as 26 March 1992 under accession lot 0144.

notes: The semi-finals. One announcer is knocked unconscious at his own desk by a wrestler unhappy with the bracket sheet, the first match turns into a seven-on-three brawl, and the second is settled by a hard hat swung against a shovel.

matches.note: A seven-on-three by the announcers’ own count. A blonde woman in leopard skin climbed the barrier and distracted Crash, and pushed Burn off the top rope as the count went down; she is revealed the following week as Shana, brought in "from the final days of the UeWF."
Molly Maguire put Flint’s own hard hat on to take Uncle Fester’s shovel — "the gong echo’s throught the arena as the hard hat cracks in half" — and the noise woke Flint up for a sunset flip on Gomez.

name: TWIW TV Tag Team Title Tournament, Round 4 (Final)

date.source: The document's own dateline; served as 31 March 1992 under accession lot 0144.

notes: The final, with a four-time former World Champion as guest announcer — who leaves the booth mid-match to go after the winners’ own seconds. The tournament crowns the first TWIW TV Tag Team Champions.

matches.note: FINAL, and the first TWIW TV Tag Team Championship. The Unknown Assailant landed a flying headbutt on Flint, who had been unconscious on the floor since Bwana put a blowgun dart in him. Five bikers came out of the third row afterwards and cleared the ring with chains.

name: WeWF Supercard #1

date.source: Report #9's own preview dates it — “The Supercard is now just four days away!” on 24 February 1991 — and Report #10 reports it in the past tense: “The Supercard took place this past Thursday.”

evidence.note: Nine matches signed and listed by name, including the Leaping Lords against the Maniacs with the Tag Team Championship on the line.
“The Maniacs beat the Leaping Lords at the Supercard” — a Tag Team Championship change this ledger carries from the report rather than from the card.
The card as it stood a week out, five matches deep, plus “MC Rapper will be rapping the National Anthem!”

notes: The league's own first Supercard. Its Tag Team Championship change and its Bjorn/Svenson “Viking King” match are both carried second-hand in the weekly reports; the card itself does not survive. The operator offered to mail a copy to anyone on the newsgroup who asked, and nobody's copy has reached this collection.

name: WeWF Supercard #2

date.source: Report #11's own announcement: “The second WeWF Supercard is scheduled for the 27th!”

evidence.note: “The second WeWF Supercard is scheduled for the 27th! Start sending your challenges now!”
Three matches signed by name, including an eight-man elimination match and an eight-man tag.
Johann “Great Dane” Svenson, in his own promo, recalls its War Games match: “Then, Bjorn, along comes SuperCard 2, and the War Games match.”

notes: Not held. Its own War Games match is recalled on camera a month later.

name: WeWF Supercard #3

date.source: Report #15's own announcement: “The 3rd Supercard is coming on the 30th of April!”, and Report #19 reports its results in the past tense.

evidence.note: “The 3rd Supercard is coming on the 30th of April!”
Two matches signed by name — a sixteen-man Triple Dome of Terror with the Hit ‘N’ Run Rabbi as referee, and a loser-drops-the-name match between the two Crushers.

Its results, read out on the following week's broadcast: “The Big Kahuna beat the Romulan Mauler in the final round to win the Iron Man Tournament, the Four Corners and the Abattoir beat Sword, Shield, Axe, Chain and the Elementals, and in the main event the General beat Frank Steel!”

notes: Not held. The first Iron Man Tournament was won here, and this ledger's own Iron Man trophy carries that bestowal on the following week's report rather than on the card.

name: WeWF October Supercard

date.source: Report #37's own announcement of 28 October 1991: “Let's see what matches have been signed for the October Supercard on Wednesday”.

evidence.note: Three matches signed by name, including a Steel Man series between the General and the Hoosiers and the Grim Reaper and the Law.
Reported in the past tense — the Law “not even showing up when they had accepted our challenge”, and “Only one Title defended at the Supercard”.

notes: Not held. The Wednesday after 28 October 1991 is 30 October; the date is recorded circa on that reading.

name: WeWF November Supercard

date.source: The Sandman's own challenge in Report #38: “the next supercard is November 28th, a WeWF tradition.”

evidence.note: “So, the next supercard is November 28th, a WeWF tradition,” with an eight-man elimination match called for by name.

The newsdesk rolls tape of a four-team elimination tag from a WeWF Supercard — the Hoosiers, the Law, the Klingons and Da Boyz — which this ledger structures on the broadcast that carries it, because the card itself is not held.

notes: Not held. A four-team elimination tag from a WeWF Supercard survives only as tape inside the newsdesk's own broadcast of 30 January 1992, and is structured there.

name: WeWF February Supercard

date.source: The newsdesk's own broadcast of 4 March 1992 rolls tape of a Supercard tag match with a losing-manager's-hair stipulation, in the same week its own regular card ran.

evidence.note: “This was a very big week in the WeWF, with both a SuperCard and a regular card” — and the Supercard tag match, Da Boyz against Flint and Steel, is rolled from tape.
The General's own post-match challenge to Matthew for a six-man “battle of the gladiators” with a five-count-pin stipulation, made the week before.

notes: Not held. Its own Da Boyz/Flint and Steel match survives only as tape inside the newsdesk's own broadcast of 4 March 1992, and is structured there.
